title: Interstate maximum
body: Alabama law permits a 70 mph maximum on interstate highways unless a different limit is posted. The number is a ceiling under favorable conditions, not a target when traffic, weather, visibility, or the roadway makes a lower speed necessary.

title: Under-21 alcohol threshold
body: Alabama applies a 0.02 percent blood-alcohol threshold to a driver under 21. That lower threshold is separate from the adult per se rule, so a young driver cannot rely on the adult number when deciding whether driving is lawful or safe.

title: Stage II night restriction
body: A Stage II driver generally may not drive from midnight through 6 a.m. Alabama lists limited exceptions, including documented travel to or from work and certain school, religious, medical, and emergency trips. A social or recreational trip does not become exempt merely because an adult knows about it.

title: Posted limit does not override conditions
body: Alabama's basic speed rule requires a reasonable and prudent speed for existing and potential hazards. A posted maximum does not authorize maintaining that speed through poor visibility, slick pavement, a curve, a hill crest, or another condition that calls for more time and space.
